ov: More than 520 species of predatory sea crustaceans, usually about 10 cm long, that live in burrows on shallow tropical and subtropical seabeds. "Smashers" club prey with a mineralised hammer and "spearers" stab it with spiny claws. Their eyes are among the most complex known.

why.dg: Nicknamed "thumb splitter": it can inflict painful wounds if handled carelessly.
why.et: Eaten in Japan (as shako sushi), Vietnam, southern China, the Philippines, Kiribati and around the Mediterranean.

len: Usually about 10 cm; up to 38 cm
rg: Shallow tropical and subtropical seas; most species live in the Indian and Pacific Oceans, from eastern Africa to Hawaii.
df: Other animals: smashers crack open crabs, snails, rock oysters and other molluscs.
fx: A club strike can reach 23 m/s, and the collapsing bubbles it leaves hit the prey a second time.
Some species pair for life, sharing a burrow with the same partner for up to 20 years.
